text: {"score":3,"justification":"Core numbers match the card (26.6% of 244, expected 5.3%, z 4.26, 0/10 below billed vs 7%, 4 of 19 no lab). The cautious, inconclusive leaning fits the evidence. However, several claims go beyond the card: a third of returned notes with duplicate text, no audit trail received, and per-sign shares (problems 21%, late 21%) cannot be verified. The headline's \"every complexity group\" is overstated, since the 0-condition group has 1 of 11 at 9.1% versus 2.2%, which is a small sample. The rationale is also internally inconsistent about whether the low-complexity claims show a pattern. Next steps are generic and omit the specific suggestions in the rationale (audit trail, duplicate-note comparison).","problems":["Claims \"a third of returned notes show duplicate text\" and an audit trail not received are not on the evidence card; they depend on tool output that is not shown here.","\"Appears in every complexity stratum\" is overstated: the 0-condition stratum rests on one 99215 claim.","The 20% low-complexity figure (13 listed claims, including 0-1 conditions) is asserted without a clear denominator, and the claim that a sicker panel \"would not readily explain\" the pattern is somewhat argumentative.","The final next_steps are generic and don't include the audit trail or the duplicate-note comparison from the rationale; they cite C0012590 and C0012607, whose depression claims with a single diagnosis are not clearly suspect.","C0012631 is described as flagged for a late note, which cannot be verified from the card.","The example list is thin: it includes an 18-year-old obesity claim and a repeated visit, with no explanation of why those support the point."]}
